preconditions.description: The number of towns n is between 3 and 100,000 inclusive.
The number of monasteries m is between 2 and n-1 inclusive.
The list of monasteries contains exactly m distinct integers.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= monastery <= n for monastery in monasteries)
preconditions.description: Each monastery is located in a town with an index between 1 and n inclusive.
There are exactly n-1 edges connecting the towns.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= ai <= n and 1 <= bi <= n and ai != bi for ai, bi, ci in edges)
preconditions.description: Each edge connects two distinct towns with indices between 1 and n inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= ci <= 1000 for ai, bi, ci in edges)
preconditions.description: Each edge has a length between 1 and 1000 inclusive.

postconditions.description: The number of unhappy pilgrims is between 0 and m inclusive.
The number of ways to destroy a town to make the maximal number of pilgrims unhappy is between 1 and n-m inclusive.

postconditions.expression: unhappy_pilgrims == max(sum(1 for pilgrim in pilgrims if all(unreachable_monastery not in reachable_monasteries[pilgrim] for unreachable_monastery in pilgrim_farther_monasteries[pilgrim])) for town in destroyable_towns)
postconditions.description: The number of unhappy pilgrims is the maximum number of pilgrims who become unhappy when any destroyable town is destroyed.

postconditions.expression: ways_to_destroy == sum(1 for town in destroyable_towns if sum(1 for pilgrim in pilgrims if all(unreachable_monastery not in reachable_monasteries[pilgrim] for unreachable_monastery in pilgrim_farther_monasteries[pilgrim])) == unhappy_pilgrims)
postconditions.description: The number of ways to destroy a town to make the maximal number of pilgrims unhappy is the count of destroyable towns that result in the maximum number of unhappy pilgrims.
